Messages.Author: Alex Harmon
Messages.Body:
Can't remember what the errata was on this so I have to ask:

Can a tapped vampire (prince) play 2nd Tradition to untap and play a
deflection (or some other reaction card) and NOT block (or attempt to
block) ??

A scenario came up tonight:

1. My predator taps to bleed me
2. I use a Telepathic Misdirection to bounce to my prey
3. My prey plays 2nd Tradition with their tapped Prince
4. My prey attempts to use a Deflection

Is 4. legal? or must the Prince attempt to block using the +2 intercept?
If stealth is added and the +2 intercept is not enough, can the Prince
then play a Deflection?

Woops, one more question:

Wasserchlos (can't remember the exact name or spelling) which is a
location requiring a ready Tremere - it says "move 1 blood from any
Tremere..." Does this mean that during the master phase, a player may
move 1 blood from potentially each and every one of their ready Tremere
onto an inactive vampire?? Or simply that any _one_ vampire (and only
one) can move a blood?

Thanks in advance.

Alex

Messages.Author: The Lasombra
Messages.Body:
In article <OizwA9AZ...@obeah.demon.co.uk>,

James Coupe <ve...@zephyr.org.uk> wrote:
> In article <39A3BC31...@white-wolf.com>, LSJ <vtesrep@white-
> wolf.com> writes
> >Dorian wrote:
> >> [Must attempt to block when playing 2nd Tradition]
> >
> >Correct.
>
> Didn't we establish during the Faceless Night scenario that during the
> stealth/intercept sequence, Deflection could be played, hence you
> wouldn't be tapped by Faceless Night for failing to block?

No, that was never established.
If you attempt to block the action,
Faceless Night will tap you when
the action completes.

If you never attempt to block, and
simply play Deflection, Deflection
is the only card that may tap you.

> Could the same be true here?
>
> e.g.
> I wake by playing 2nd Tradition.
> Acting Methuselah plays no effects in response.
> I play Deflection.

You are attempting to block when you play the 2nd Tradition. If you
are attempting to block, you must fail to block before you can do
anything else.

Therefore, you may not play Deflection/Redirection/Telepathic
Misdirection, after playing a 2nd Tradition, unless the stealth of the
bleed is at 3 or higher, or if the acting minion plays a superior Elder
Impersonation (causing the reacting minion to be unable to block).

See the New Card Text from 23rd June 1998 Rules Team Rulings:

Second Tradition: Domain, The:
New card text:
"Requires ready Prince or Justicar. +2 intercept. Also usable by a
tapped Prince or Justicar, even if intercept is not yet needed, to
untap and attempt to block with +2 intercept."

You must attempt to block if you play a 2nd Tradition. Similarly, a
Prince or Justicar may not use 2nd Tradition to untap, if the acting
minion played a Seduction naming the P/J.

Carpe Noctem.

>

> stealth/intercept sequence, Deflection could be played, hence you

>
> e.g.
> I wake by playing 2nd Tradition.
> Acting Methuselah plays no effects in response.
> I play Deflection.
>

> One option would be to declare that since the Acting Methuselah had
> played no cards to increase his/her stealth, you would go into combat
> immediately. However, that would seem to break rule 1.6.1.5

No. If the block succeeds, you cannot play deflection.

For instance, you cannot attempt to block a bleed in the hopes
that the acting minion will increase his stealth before you
deflect and then deflect even if he doesn't increase the bleed.

The only reaction cards you can play at that point (successfully
blocking an action) are cards like Obedience.

Messages.Author: LSJ
Messages.Body:
James Coupe wrote:
> The Lasombra <TheLa...@hotmail.com> writes
> >You are attempting to block when you play the 2nd Tradition. If you
> >are attempting to block, you must fail to block before you can do
> >anything else.
>
> You were attempting to block in the Faceless Night situation.
>
> If you had failed to block, you would be tapped - but you could play
> Deflection before that happened.

Right. If the Faceless Night minion has more stealth than the would-be
blocker, the blocker hasn't yet failed to block - he gets the opportunity
to, for example, generate more intercept before becoming tapped.

So the sequence there is:

A: V1 bleeds B
A: <no futher modifiers>
B: V2 attempts to block
A: V1 plays superior Faceless Night
A: <no further modifiers>

At this point, the block is not succeeding, so the blocking minion/Meth
can do several things:

1. Nothing. Allow the bleed through. B is tapped.
2. Something. Increase Intercept or play Deflection, for example.

> In the Faceless Night situation, you did not have to fail to block.
>
> LSJ seemed to make it clear that Deflection could be played during the
> stealth/intercept time then. If it was played afterwards, you would be
> tapped by Faceless Night. I wonder why it cannot be played in the same
> timing slot here.

Deflection is not playable when the block is succeeding - by the time
the blocking Methuselah gets the opportunity to play it, she's already
facing combat:

A: V1 bleeds B
A: <no futher modifiers>
B: V2 attempts to block (possibly by playing 2nd Tradition, for instance)
A: Block succeeds
A: <no further modifiers>

B cannot attempt to deflect at this time.

In article <8o1kfd$n6a$1...@nnrp1.deja.com>,


The tapping from Faceless Night only takes effect if the action that FN
gives stealth to, succeeds. At this point that action hasn't succeeded
since a blocking minion always gets the opportunity to play more
intercept when the action minion played stealth. So if he has the
opportunity to play intercept (which is a reaction card) then obviously
the tapping effect of FN hasn't taken place yet, which also means that
you could play a Deflection instead of intercept.
